messages:
Samar (support): :rotating_light: multiple customers hitting 401s after the scheduled key rollout. First report at ~08:12 UTC. Example reproducer from customer:

Samar (support): ```
curl -i -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_OLD_abc123' https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat.completions -d '{"model":"gpt-x","prompt":"hi"}'
HTTP/1.1 401 Unauthorized
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"invalid_api_key","code":"auth.invalid_key"}
```

Samar (support): Affected: 3 self-serve PLG accounts and 1 enterprise (acme-inc). Customer says they were on a long-lived key that we rotated. They expected backward compatibility during migration.

Alice M (eng-security): On it. Any change logs from the key-rotation job? Was there a revocation call to KMS or we switched pointers only?

Ben K (eng-platform): Deploy Bot shows key-roll job ran at 08:10 UTC. Job log link: https://ci.redwood.internal/rolls/4721

Deploy Bot: [info] key-roll/4721 started by scheduler at 2026-03-14T08:10:02Z
Deploy Bot: [info] created new key sk_NEW_z9
Deploy Bot: [error] attempted to mark previous keys as "deprecated" then revoke: KMS revoke failed with 500 for key sk_OLD_abc123
Deploy Bot: [info] roll finished with warnings

Carla R (infra): If revoke failed but we marked as deprecated, there might be a brief window where our auth layer rejects both old and new key formats. Looking into auth gateway logs now.

Marta (oncall): Pasting auth-gateway sample log around 08:11:

Marta (oncall): ```
2026-03-14T08:11:15Z auth-gw request id=xyz token=sk_OLD_abc123 -> lookup -> status=DEPRECATED
2026-03-14T08:11:15Z auth-gw policy check -> allowed=False -> respond 401
2026-03-14T08:11:15Z auth-gw cache miss -> fetch keys -> returned [] (KMS 500)
```

Alice M (eng-security): That cache miss + KMS 500 explains it. The auth-gateway treats DEPRECATED keys as not accepted while KMS was unavailable to confirm previous valid fingerprint. So regression introduced when we tightened deprecation semantics in the rollout code.

Samar (support): Customers want immediate mitigation. Can we re-enable acceptance of deprecated keys until KMS is healthy? Need a short-term toggle.

Carla R (infra): Yes. Two options:
- Hotfix to auth-gateway to accept DEPRECATED keys if KMS returns error (config flip)
- Roll back the key-roll flag to avoid deprecation state

Ben K (eng-platform): Rolling back the deprecation step is faster. I can trigger rollback to previous key state for all affected projects. It will re-enable old key handling without touching code.

Alice M (eng-security): We should also throttle the rotation job and create a follow-up to fix the deprecation semantics. Short-term rollback now + revert the revoke until KMS SLA is resolved.

Marta (oncall): I'll coordinate the rollback. Initiating now. ETA ~4m.

Incidents Bot: :white_check_mark: rollback:keys/4721 initiated by Marta (oncall) at 2026-03-14T08:18:02Z

Marta (oncall): Rollback complete. Monitoring logs for successful auth checks.

Marta (oncall): Post-rollback sample:

Marta (oncall): ```
2026-03-14T08:19:21Z auth-gw request id=abc token=sk_OLD_abc123 -> lookup -> status=ACTIVE
2026-03-14T08:19:21Z auth-gw policy check -> allowed=True -> respond 200
```

Samar (support): Customer confirmation: acme-inc says traffic resumed and 401s stopped. Thanks team. :pray:

Alice M (eng-security): Root cause summary so far: key-rotation job changed deprecation handling to be strict (deprecated == reject). If KMS lookup fails during the window, auth-gateway treated keys as invalid. KMS returned transient 500 during revoke, causing an operational window where neither old nor new keys validated.

Ben K (eng-platform): Action items I will own:
- Re-run rollout with stepped canary and no immediate revoke (platform-issue-#2347)
- Add rollback automation to undo deprecation quickly (PR queued)

Alice M (eng-security): Action items I will own:
- Revert change that made DEPRECATED keys strictly invalid and add fallback (auth-gw PR)
- Add unit + integration tests to simulate KMS failures

Carla R (infra): Action items I will own:
- Work with KMS vendor on the 500s during our window and review retry/backoff (infra-ticket-#889)

Samar (support): I'll follow up with customers with timeline and ETA for postmortem. Logging incident for billing/sla checks.

Incidents Bot: :memo: Incident created INC-2026-0314-01 assigned to "eng-security" and "eng-platform". Severity: P2. Link: https://incidents.redwood/internal/INC-2026-0314-01

Marta (oncall): We'll keep the thread updated. Postmortem required within 72 hours. Marking this resolved for now since rollback restored service. :thumbsup:

Samar (support): Closing customer-facing alert. Will reopen if any regression.

Alice M (eng-security): Note for postmortem: include exact timeline, customer impact, and concrete deploy guardrails (canary %, KMS health gating). Also recommend a brief communications note for sales/CS.

Ben K (eng-platform): A quick mitigation doc snippet for support so they can triage similar reports:

Ben K (eng-platform): ```
Repro steps for 401 after key rotation:
1) Check deploy logs for key-roll job id
2) Check auth-gateway logs for token lookup status
3) If KMS 5xx seen, trigger rollback: keys/ROLLBACK <job-id>
4) Notify eng-platform + eng-security
```

Samar (support): Saved. Thanks everyone. :lock:

Incidents Bot: :white_check_mark: incident INC-2026-0314-01 marked RESOLVED at 2026-03-14T08:26:30Z (mitigated by rollback)."
